posts.body_html:
Question on the name "Green Monster." I haven't been able to find where Bill Scholl has registered this beautiful plant. (If a description is out there, can someone provide a link?) In the absence of an official description, can any AF minor x leuco be called "Green Monster" as long as it has the same appearance?

I ask because I purchased some AF minor x leuco seed last fall, and about 8 of the seedlings are now 8-10" tall and so far look just like the pictures in this thread and others I've found online of "legitimate divisions"(?) of Bill's original hybrid. (A few seedlings tended more toward the appearance of the leuco parent and are about twice as tall, and very attractive in their own right.) But the great thing about growing Sarrs from seed is that you often end up with more plants than you need/want/have space for, and by this time next year I'll probably be sharing my excess plants. As for my own growlist, I'm happy to just call them S. x excellens "antho-free", but what's to keep the people I share my extra plants with from calling them "Green Monster"? (Yes, I would explain the origin of my plants.) Would the same apply for seeds from "Green Monster" x self as long as the appearance is the same?

I'm just trying to better understand the naming conventions, not create a controversy (nor am I trying to prod Bill to register a description, if he hasn't already!). I'm perfectly happy with my generic S. x excellens "antho-free".


(Picture taken 10/25/22 shortly after I'd moved them out of the growbox and into their outdoor home.)

posts.body_html: jgreen1025 Only plants obtained via vegetative division from the named cultivar can be called ‘Green Monster’. All plants grown from seed should be listed by whatever cross created them unless you feel the need to give them a specific name. You of course shouldn’t name them Green Monster. Green Monster x Self will produce seedlings that are not genetically the same as Green Monster so should not be named Green Monster as well.

In the absence of an official description, can any AF minor x leuco be called "Green Monster" as long as it has the same appearance?

Regardless of whether a cultivar is registered or not, "look alike" plants recreated by making similar crosses are not the same as the named clonal cultivar.  If any prove exceptional they can be introduced under new names.  The only cases in which the same name should apply to seed grown plants is if the cultivar name is assigned to a select cross known to come true from seed or a line bred true to type variety.  Most Sarracenia cultivars are clonal and not the latter.
